recipes.name: Red and Green Christmas Jalapeno Jelly

steps.text: Remove stems, veins and most of the seeds of the bell and jalapeno peppers. Mince peppers in a food processor.
In a 5-quart pot over high heat, combine bell peppers, jalapenos, sugar and vinegar. Bring to a rolling boil; boil for 3 minutes. Remove from heat and cool for 5 minutes.
Stirring constantly, add the pectin and let mixture continue to cool for 2 minutes more. Now stir for 1 minute.
Pour into hot, sterilized jars and top with sterilized lids. Secure lids with bands and allow jars to cool slowly, creating a vacuum seal.

raw_recipe.headline: Red and Green Christmas Jalapeno Jelly
raw_recipe.description: This is a beautiful jelly of red bell peppers and green jalapenos. It’s a perfect relish to many holiday favorites, or serve it with cream cheese on a cracker.

review.reviewBody: I can't say anything more that hasn't been said about how good this recipe is. I tried this last year for christmas as a newbie canner. (I still am a newbie canner). I searched the reviews and wished someone had quickly explained the "canning" process, but sadly found none. So I wanted to put my 2 cents in and try to feed some info for those like me who are scared to try. ( I may make some canners cringe, so please feel free to correct me!) This recipe makes 4 12 oz jars or 6 8 oz. I used 2 medium red peppers and 5-6 med-large jalapenos. I washed the jars and lids in hot soapy water and put the jars in a very large pot and covered with water. I put it on high heat until the water simmered (about 180 degrees) and turned the flame down to keep it at a simmer. Then I started cooking the jelly. When it was almost ready, I use a pair of large tongs to take out the jars and poured in the jelly, leaving 1/4 inch space on top. I then plopped on the lid and screwed the screw top on and stood it back in the pot and boiled for 5 minutes and removed. I then did the mentioned flip trick -- flipping four times, once a half hour, to ensure evenly distrubuted peppers. I made four batches for this christmas. It's a great last minute gift when you forgot someone and great when visiting. Thank you for the great recipe!

This is my first time to actually write a review. It was so good and am excited to give as gifts. After reading the reviews, I used 2 red peppers, 5 jalapeños, leaving the seeds in 2. (I’m not that adventurous with spicy and it was perfect for us.) Diced in processor and let drain in colander. When I added the liquid pectin, I put back on heat, stirring constantly. I used a thermometer til it hit 220 degrees. (The second batch, I broke it so had to eyeball it.) I read the canning process and had jars simmering in water until ready to go. When done, I put back in water for 10 minutes. I heard the lids pop after about 15 min sitting on counter. I did not need to flip, peppers stayed distributed.

I doubled the batch which made 26 four ounce jars for Christmas gifts. 
The proportions I used were 3 medium sized red peppers, 4 jalapenos, 4 pouches of liquid pectin, 10 cups sugar, and 3 cups apple cider vinegar.
I seeded the red peppers but only cut off the stem of the jalapeno and the heat was good for us.
I changed the method slightly as I can a lot and have never taken the pot off the heat prior to adding the pectin.
I brought the pot to a boil, added the pectin, boiled for 3 minutes, turned off the heat and skimmed the foam from the pot. 
I filled the hot jars and placed the snap lids on, I processed them for 5 minutes in a hot water bath, all my jars sealed and set even though I doubled the recipe.
I used my largest stock pot which was perfect.
Do not add onions or garlic, it throws off the acidity of the recipe which can lead to botulism, with canning you need to follow the ingredients to make sure you have the corect ph to kill any bacteria.

I was so excited to make something different and fun (and delicious) with all the jalapeño and Fresno peppers from my garden! Thanks to all the reviews that helped me do things right - my first batch turned out perfect! I scraped the pot with a spatula and ate it - didn’t want to waste any!! I only used 1 bell pepper from my garden (it was yellow) and then all the rest (over a cup) were jalapeño and Fresno peppers. Thank you to 1cookieangel for your suggestion about using the tea ball for the veins & seeds - it worked so well - it really has a great zing to it! Also thank you to oyerb for your suggestion to use the candy thermometer and boil to 220 after adding the Certo - it set up perfectly! This turned out great, it was pretty easy and it’s going to be so fun to give as Christmas gifts!! Yay!

I made this Red and Green Christmas Jalapeno Jelly and it turned out beautifully. I doubled the recipe and cut the sugar from 10 cups to 8 cups. I also substituted the liquid pectin and used Sure Jell premium fruit pectin instead. Because I had doubled the recipe I then used two packages of 1.75 oz. After sterilized jars are filled with hot jelly, I then process lidded jars in hot water and then allow to cool and you will hear the lids ping as the sealing process takes place. When jars are filled and sealed follow the guideline in flipping every 20 minutes for next hour, this will suspend the red bell pepper and jalapeno bits evenly. My family and friends will polish off a bottle with cream cheese and crackers as soon as it is opened. Delicious!

My daughter and I tried this recipe for the first time following recipe. But instead of measuring the peppers we used 6 jalapeño (reserving one for garnish) and one large red bell pepper. We only cleaned seeds and ribs from the bell pepper and one jalapeno pepper for garniah...but left the seeds and ribs in the other five jalapeños and minced in a food processor. Also since we were giving as gifts, after we filled the jars, we put jars in a water bath for ten minutes just to insure the seal. Also before putting on the lids, garnish each jar of jam with some diced jalapeño. The vinegar gives the jam a nice yellow and the green and red peppers make it very Christmasy. You dont taste the vinegar at all. Everyone who tried it loves it. Well except for my husband. We're still laughing heartily over the faces he made trying to get the cracker, cream cheese, and jam past his tongue. Our daughter had to give him the jug of milk to drink....really, unless you put the jam alone on your tongue, its not as hot as he portrayed it to be....he just likes plain old boring food. LOL. The seeds give it a nice after bite. Caution! When prepping the peppers for the food processor, wear two pairs of food prep gloves or your hands will be stinging for quite a while. Make sure you read the ounces on the liquid pectin pouch or you'll get too little or too much. Six ounces is perfect. Sets almost immediately.

I love it. I used 1 average red pepper (1 c) and 2 big jalapeno (1/2 c). I left half of the seeds in jalapeno. I followed the advice of Teri MC and processed in hot water bath and boiled the filled jars for 5 minutes. I also flipped the jars every 30 minutes for about 2 hours. I have hunted for a good pepper jelly for a long time, and this one is perfect; not too hot but with a little zing and lots of flavor.

I just finished 5 batches perfectly, beautiful color with red and green specks throughout and every jar set up. The recipe makes 5 8oz jars with a little to pour into a bowl. I did this so I could see that it set up properly then just covered and placed in the fridge for myself.

Here's what I did differently. I followed the ingredients pretty much exactly except that I used 3/4 cup of Jalapeno instead of 1/2 cup and left half the seeds and placenta in so I would have more heat. I used a 2 cup Kitchenaid chopper to mince the peppers. I brought the mixture to a rolling boil while still stirring for 1 minute following the directions on the pectin sheet for pepper relish (pretty close to pepper jelly). Removed from heat and added ONE packet of liquid pectin (also per Ball pectin direction sheet included in the box of 2 packets) returned to a full rolling boil for exactly one minute...set a timer. I then removed from heat and poured into sterilized jars and did a water bath for 5 mins. I did 5 batches, 25 8oz jars all sealed, beautiful amber color (did not add food coloring but you can) and ready to enjoy. I did turn them to evenly distribute the flecks.

This recipe is wonderful. I get rave reviews and it is easy to change the heat. I use about a cup of red pepper chopped in a food processor, if the juice separates, I don't add it but I also don't use paper towels to get the liquid out. I use about 5 large jalapeños, with the seeds of 2 of them. Comes out wonderful. I use 1 and a half packages of liquid pectin per batch, and have done a double batch this way with success. I also put the jars in a hot water bath for 5 minutes because I was having problems with the jars sealing properly. If doing a double batch, I extend the cooling time after removing from heat to about 10 minutes, not sure if that makes a difference or not.

It's so pretty! My first time canning anything and all my jars sealed! I love that "pop"! Admittedly, I haven't opened one of the jars yet, but a "finger-through-the-remnants-in-the-pan" test tasted great. I got 12 4-oz jars from this recipe.

After reading the reviews and doing a lot of research online, I did the following:

* Followed exact quantities per the recipe. Per one of the reviews, I had the peppers at room temperture. Not sure that helped with the disbursement of the peppers, but the peppers are suspended beautifully without having to do the flip tip mentioned in some reviews. Another tip I followed was to put the veins and seeds of a few of the jalepeno peppers (maybe 4) in a tea ball and put in the jelly while cooking. You get the heat but can easily remove the seeds and veins from the final product so your jelly looks beautiful. 
* After buying the wrong kind of pectin...TWICE...I finally found liquid pectin at my local grocery. Research online said not to substitute the power for the liquid. The jelly was setting up before I got all the jars filled. I'm in NC so didn't have to make any altitude adjustments. The liquid pectin kept the jelly crystal clear. I understand that powder pectin may have caused the jelly to be cloudy.
* After filling all the jars, I processed them in a boiling water bath for 5 minutes.

The jelly looks to have set in the cooled jars. The jelly is a beautiful clear amber color with red and green peppers suspended throughtout.

Rating on taste: 5 
Instructions get: 2 for lacking critical parts
Great finished product but... the instructions are lacking. It is 2 3oz packets of liquid pectin. After which it needs to be placed back on the heat and boil for 1 min. Otherwise it will probably not set. Luckily I read a number of the reviews that mentioned these steps were left out. Great tasting hot jelly though when done correctly!

I made this yesterday. I used multi colored peppers and 3 large jalapenos with seeds. It is hot and sweet. It is so good I am putting in on everything. I was worried it was not going to set u[p but when I put it in the fridge it set up.

We have been making this for Christmas for the last 15 years and everyone loves it. Our note: we use 1/4 cup chopped green bell and 1/4 cup chopped jalapeno instead of the 1/2 cup chopped jalapeno. (some people in my family don't like all the heat)
It has become our regular not just Christmas jelly , very simple and easy to make - great tasting .

This is my 2nd year making red pepper jelly and my 1st time with this recipe. I've done 2 separate batches and they worked out great. Taste perfect. Easy to follow just have everything out that you need and a large area to work in. Things come together quick. I plan to make a 3rd batch and increase the jalapeno so i have mild and hot. I'm giving away jars for Christmas.
tiny tiny alteration of 1.5 cups of red pepper as i had extra. thanks to bernardin liquid pectin it set up nicely. excellent flavor!

This recipe is perfect just the way it is. I don't understand in other reviews the need to flip the jars. Mine is thick enough by the time it goes into the jars everything stays where it belongs. No need to take a simple recipe and make it difficult. Beautiful and delicious!

Huge hit! Great use for the jalapeños from the garden. The color of the jelly is beautiful. We never have any leftover jars. Completely agree with the comments about blotting to get excess moisture from the peppers and boiling to 220 degrees. Delicious!
Have made this recipe every year and it’s a winner every time. Have used sure-jell also instead of liquid pectin and it makes it thicker.
I made it with two red peppers, one green and 8 red thai peppers (seeds and vines removed), pulsed in a food processor. I added a pinch of garlic and onion powder. Excellent!
